prompt:
A user has already approved a memory edit. You are reconciling native facts extracted from a changed version of the SAME source. The ledger is trusted user intent, not a suggested extraction. Classify every supplied fact ID exactly once; do not write or rewrite any facts.
keep: unrelated fact, already compatible with the accepted edit, or a genuinely NEW explicit event that supersedes the old statement (move, replacement, reassignment). An edit to historical evidence is not a ban on future changes.
replay: this fact restates the original targeted claim, without new independent information beyond that original claim. The application will substitute the accepted text verbatim (or omit if empty).
conflict: the source changed the targeted value in contradiction to the accepted edit, with NO explicit new event. The application will use the trusted safe remainder, flag the conflict, and not choose either value.
merge: the fact mixes the targeted old claim or attribution with independently useful NEW/other information that the accepted text would lose. It needs a local edit. This includes a former personal number now assigned to a company: the company/new number stays, but do not keep the forgotten former personal attribution.
Classify only the targeted entity/relationship; same words belonging to a different person or object are not the target. Returning an exact old value is replay, not conflict, even if it differs from the accepted correction. Changed unrelated statements are keep. Do not treat all changed wording as a conflict.
mergePrompt: Apply only the user's approved memory edit to this ONE native fact. Preserve every independent current detail and its person/object/time. Use the original and accepted statements as the edit before/after example; do not copy the accepted statement if it loses newly added useful details. Remove forgotten attribution even from historical clauses; retain new owners and facts. Return one complete grammatical factual statement, or empty only if nothing unrelated remains. Do not add a fact not supported by the native fact or the approved user edit. This is not a request to resolve a conflict; that was handled separately.
note: Ledger replacement/remainder are synthetic user-approved edits, not claimed automatic extraction or successful first-edit generation. Actual native facts reused from previous recorded runs.
